{{Short description|Characterizes homeomorphisms of a compact orientable surface}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Thurston's [[classification theorem]]''' characterizes [[homeomorphism]]s of a [[compact surface|compact orientable surface]].  [[William Thurston]]'s theorem completes the work initiated by {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Jakob Nielsen (mathematician)|first=Jakob |last=Nielsen|year=1944}}.

Given a homeomorphism ''f''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''S''&nbsp;→&nbsp;''S'', there is a map ''g'' [[Homotopy#Isotopy|isotopic]] to ''f'' such that at least one of the following holds:
* ''g'' is periodic, i.e. some power of ''g'' is the identity;
* ''g'' preserves some finite union of disjoint simple closed curves on ''S'' (in this case, ''g'' is called ''reducible''); or
* ''g'' is [[pseudo-Anosov map|pseudo-Anosov]].

The case where ''S'' is a [[torus]] (i.e., a surface whose [[Genus (mathematics)|genus]] is one) is handled separately (see [[torus bundle]]) and was known before Thurston's work. If the genus of ''S'' is two or greater, then ''S'' is naturally [[hyperbolic geometry|hyperbolic]], and the tools of [[Teichmüller space|Teichmüller theory]] become useful.  In what follows, we assume ''S'' has genus at least two, as this is the case Thurston considered. (Note, however, that the cases where ''S'' has [[Boundary (topology)|boundary]] or is not [[orientable]] are definitely still of interest.)

The three types in this classification are '''not''' mutually exclusive, though a ''pseudo-Anosov'' homeomorphism is never ''periodic'' or ''reducible''.  A ''reducible'' homeomorphism ''g'' can be further analyzed by cutting the surface along the preserved union of simple closed curves ''Γ''.  Each of the resulting compact surfaces ''with [[manifold|boundary]]'' is acted upon by some power (i.e. [[function composition|iterated composition]]) of ''g'', and the classification can again be applied to this homeomorphism.

==The mapping class group for surfaces of higher genus==
Thurston's classification applies to homeomorphisms of orientable surfaces of genus ≥ 2, but the type of a homeomorphism only depends on its associated element of the [[mapping class group]] ''Mod(S)''.  In fact, the proof of the classification theorem leads to a [[canonical form|canonical]] representative of each mapping class with good geometric properties.  For example:
* When ''g'' is periodic, there is an element of its mapping class that is an [[isometry]] of a [[hyperbolic geometry|hyperbolic structure]] on ''S''.
* When ''g'' is [[pseudo-Anosov]], there is an element of its mapping class that preserves a pair of [[Transversality (mathematics)|transverse]] singular [[foliation]]s of ''S'', stretching the leaves of one (the ''unstable'' foliation) while contracting the leaves of the other (the ''stable'' foliation).

==Mapping tori==
Thurston's original motivation for developing this classification was to find geometric structures on ''mapping tori'' of the type predicted by the [[Geometrization conjecture]].  The [[mapping torus]] ''M<sub>g</sub>'' of a homeomorphism ''g'' of a surface ''S'' is the [[3-manifold]] obtained from ''S'' × [0,1] by gluing ''S'' × {0} to ''S'' × {1} using ''g''. If S has genus at least two, the geometric structure of ''M<sub>g</sub>'' is related to the type of ''g'' in the classification as follows:
* If ''g'' is periodic, then ''M<sub>g</sub>'' has an ''H''<sup>2</sup> × R structure;
* If ''g'' is reducible, then ''M<sub>g</sub>'' has [[incompressible surface|incompressible]] [[torus|tori]], and should be cut along these tori to yield pieces that each have geometric structures (the [[JSJ decomposition]]);
* If ''g'' is [[pseudo-Anosov map|pseudo-Anosov]], then ''M<sub>g</sub>'' has a [[hyperbolic geometry|hyperbolic]] (i.e. ''H''<sup>3</sup>) structure.

The first two cases are comparatively easy, while the existence of a hyperbolic structure on the mapping torus of a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism is a deep and difficult theorem (also due to [[William Thurston|Thurston]]).  The hyperbolic 3-manifolds that arise in this way are called ''fibered'' because they are [[surface bundle over the circle|surface bundles over the circle]], and these manifolds are treated separately in the proof of Thurston's [[geometrization conjecture|geometrization theorem]] for [[Haken manifold]]s.  Fibered hyperbolic 3-manifolds have a number of interesting and pathological properties; for example, Cannon and Thurston showed that the surface subgroup of the arising [[Kleinian group]] has [[limit set]] which is a [[space-filling curve|sphere-filling curve]].

==Fixed point classification==
The three types of surface homeomorphisms are also related to the [[dynamical system|dynamics]] of the mapping class group Mod(''S'') on the [[Teichmüller space]] ''T''(''S'').  Thurston introduced a [[compactification (mathematics)|compactification]] of ''T''(''S'') that is homeomorphic to a closed ball, and to which the action of Mod(''S'') extends naturally.  The type of an element ''g'' of the mapping class group in the Thurston classification is related to its fixed points when acting on the compactification of ''T''(''S''):
* If ''g'' is periodic, then there is a fixed point within ''T''(''S''); this point corresponds to a [[hyperbolic geometry|hyperbolic structure]] on ''S'' whose [[isometry group]] contains an element isotopic to ''g'';
* If ''g'' is [[pseudo-Anosov]], then ''g'' has no fixed points in ''T''(''S'') but has a pair of fixed points on the Thurston boundary; these fixed points correspond to the ''stable'' and ''unstable'' foliations of ''S'' preserved by ''g''.
* For some reducible mapping classes ''g'', there is a single fixed point on the Thurston boundary; an example is a [[Dehn twist|multi-twist]] along a [[pants decomposition]] ''Γ''.  In this case the fixed point of ''g'' on the Thurston boundary corresponds to ''Γ''.

This is reminiscent of the classification of [[hyperbolic geometry|hyperbolic]] [[isometries]] into ''elliptic'', ''parabolic'', and ''hyperbolic'' types (which have fixed point structures similar to the ''periodic'', ''reducible'', and ''pseudo-Anosov'' types listed above).
